pl-l2d41c4-d1e108.summary: Infers that if every mortal sin is voluntary and evil will is mortal sin, evil will is itself voluntary sin.

pl-l2d41c4-d1e111.summary: Cites Augustine: what is so much in the will as the will itself? So evil will is rightly called voluntary sin; will is the first cause of sinning, or no sin is; sin is rightly imputed only to the sinner, and so only to the will.
claims: Will is the first cause of sin.
Sin is imputed to the will.

pl-l2d41c4-d1e114.summary: States this concerns actual and mortal sin, and that Augustine, as he says in the Retractationes, meant only that will is that by which one sins and lives rightly.
claims: Will is the principle of sin and right living.

pl-l2d41c4.summary: If every mortal sin is voluntary, and evil will is mortal sin, then evil will is itself voluntary sin, since nothing is so in the will as the will itself. Augustine: will is the first cause of sinning, or no sin is; sin is imputed only to the sinner, and so only to the will. This concerns actual mortal sin; Augustine meant only that will is that by which one sins and lives rightly.
claims: Evil will is itself voluntary sin.
Nothing is so much in the will as the will itself.
Will is the first cause of sinning.
Sin is rightly imputed only to the will.
